item.title: The Southern Taurid meteor shower will bring rare fireballs tonight
item.description:
The Southern Taurid meteor shower produces only about five meteors an hour but is known for bright fireballs from marble- to boulder-sized debris shed by comet 2P/Encke, with viewing expected to be best around midnight Thursday and the peak estimated around 3 p.m. ET on Nov. 5, according to EarthSky. NASA's Bill Cooke said "when you see one, you'll remember it" and advised finding a dark spot and giving eyes at least half an hour to adjust without a phone, while astronomer Bethany Cobb Kung suggests locating Orion's belt and looking to the right toward Taurus. Cooke said Earth is predicted to pass through a denser swarm of Taurid debris in 2032, describing the present as "a lull before the thunderstorms occur."

item.title: Southern Utah couple accused of abusing young daughter
item.description:
Trevor Dean Noffsinger, 22, and Mariah Faith Calapp, 21, of Cedar City were booked into the Iron County Jail on Tuesday for investigation of aggravated child abuse after an investigation that began in February, when doctors found their 4-month-old daughter had clavicle and rib fractures in different stages of healing along with grip-pattern bruising that medical staff deemed non-accidental. item.title: 'It wasn't just a home': Flooding displaces generations of a family near Bluff
item.description:

One grandmother and four cousins are now in Atcitty's basement, bringing her household to 10, while another grandmother is in an RV park cabin near Blanding, and the family doesn't know whether the homes will be livable given worries about water under the structures and mold. Atcitty, whose own parents lost their home there in a 2003 flood, said "It wasn't just a home that they lost," and has started a GoFundMe for the family.

item.title: A 24-year-old running the NYC marathon collapsed 2 miles from the finish line and died
item.description:
Rachel Apa, 24, of Lewisberry, Pennsylvania, collapsed a couple of miles short of the finish in her first New York City Marathon on Sunday and died at a hospital; the medical examiner is still investigating, though her father told the New York Times the cause was rhabdomyolysis, a rare condition in which skeletal muscle breaks down and poisons the body. Mount Sinai nephrologist Doug Farrell, who documented 24 rhabdo cases at the unusually hot 2022 race, said heat speeds muscle breakdown, though Sunday's temperatures hovered in the mid-60s. Emory sports cardiologist Jonathan Kim said deaths from rhabdo "would be really, really rare", noting that heart attack is the most common cause of cardiac arrest in marathons and that runners' chance of dying from sudden cardiac arrest fell by half from 2010 to 2023.

item.title: JetBlue raises baggage fees a second time as jet fuel prices stay elevated
item.description:
JetBlue has raised checked bag fees for the second time this year, so most economy passengers on tickets bought on or after Nov. 3 will pay at least $50 each way for a first bag, up from $39, and as much as $70 when paying within 24 hours of a peak-period departure. The airline's March increase helped set off bag-fee hikes at Delta, United, American and Southwest, and JetBlue said in the spring that the increases help offset higher operating costs while keeping base fares competitive. Jet fuel prices have stayed elevated because the unresolved Iran war has largely restricted traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, and JetBlue expects its average fuel price to reach $4.64 a gallon in the final three months of the year, up 85% from a year earlier.

item.title: Sen. Riebe says she won't resign, pushes back on misconduct allegations
item.description:
Utah state Sen. Kathleen Riebe of Cottonwood Heights said Wednesday "I am not going to resign" after fellow Senate Democrats voted to remove her from their caucus and called for her resignation, citing an investigation they say found workplace harassment and discrimination. Riebe said she was not allowed to review the report or invited to meet before the vote, and told KSL she believes the matter stems from concerns she raised about a legislative staffer allegedly doing campaign work for Senate Minority Leader Luz Escamilla, who did not immediately respond. She also questioned the timing of the announcement, released late Tuesday just before polls closed on a big election night for Democrats.

item.title: Davis County man who wanted to 'go out in a hail of glory' faces felony charges
item.description:
Kelly Scott Dicus, 43, of Clearfield, is charged with aggravated kidnapping and other domestic violence-related counts after charging documents say he appeared inside his estranged wife's home shortly after midnight Oct. 9, days after she served him an eviction notice, took her phone and kept her from leaving while a gun in his lap pointed toward her. According to the charges, he said that if the children called police he would "make sure he took officers with him," and police say he later brandished a gun at officers during an armed standoff in Syracuse and was shot. Police asked that Dicus be held until trial as a "lethal threat", and Syracuse police said more charges may follow once the officer-involved shooting investigation concludes.

item.title: Utah House Republicans may lose supermajority for first time in decades
item.description:
Utah Republicans appear on track to lose their two-thirds supermajority in the state House for the first time this century, with 15 sitting GOP lawmakers trailing their challengers on Wednesday and the caucus possibly shrinking from 61 seats to as few as 44, which would leave it unable to override vetoes or propose constitutional amendments without Democratic votes; Senate Majority Leader Kirk Cullimore also trailed Democrat Shana Anderson by more than 4,000 votes. Incumbents blamed a national wave compounded by their own missteps, with Rep. Matt MacPherson calling the decision to put Amendment B on the ballot a likely strategic error, though Rep. Norm Thurston, trailing by nearly 600 votes, noted that only about half of Utah County's ballots had been counted. Taylor Morgan of Morgan May Public Affairs described "the blue bludgeoning" reaching Utah, while BYU political scientist Adam Brown attributed the losses chiefly to dissatisfaction with the Trump administration, saying down-ballot races are driven by "what's happening at the top".

item.title: NASA space telescope plunges to Earth after 2 decades studying cosmic explosions
item.description:
NASA's Swift Observatory reentered the atmosphere near Indonesia on Wednesday, ending a study of gamma ray bursts and exploding stars that was planned for two years but lasted 22, after solar activity dragged down its orbit and a robotic orbit-boost attempt by Katalyst Space failed when that craft came down in September. NASA anticipated that some denser pieces of the 1 1/2-ton spacecraft would survive reentry. The agency is now asking private companies how they might boost, upgrade or safely deorbit the Hubble Space Telescope, which recent analyses expect to come down by the mid-2030s, and Administrator Jared Isaacman said the telescope "still has important science ahead of it".

item.title: 'The Chosen' is fully funded. What's next?
item.description:
Come and See, the nonprofit behind The Chosen, has reached the $78 million goal to fund the seventh and final season with help from more than 86,000 supporters in 175 countries, and can now focus on reaching 1 billion people and translating all seven seasons into 600 languages at about $75,000 per season per language. Come and See's Stacey Baxter said "Now the work is to take it to the world," noting that the series app drew 2.2 million international users in October, compared with 1.6 million in the United States. Season 6 premieres Nov. 15 on Prime Video, and the first season already holds a Guinness World Records title as the most-translated television season, in 125 languages.

item.title: 'We have kids,' victim told gunman before being fatally shot during robbery
item.description:
Ryley Jilberto Avila, 26, of Taylorsville, has been charged with murder, aggravated robbery and other counts in the Oct. 24 killing of Abraham Martinez, 24, in a West Valley City IHOP parking lot, where charges say Avila showed up "under the guise of buying cocaine" without money and pulled a gun. Martinez was in the back seat next to his children, ages 2 and 4, and his girlfriend heard him repeat "We have kids" before Avila allegedly shot him in the head inside the car and fired a second round as the car drove away. A man who was with Avila told police he suspected a robbery but knew of no plan to shoot anyone, and Avila was arrested at a Taylorsville apartment with help from a SWAT team.

item.title: Democratic sweep of Congress ushers in new era; Trump acknowledges impact of the Iran war
item.description:
Democrats won unusually wide majorities in both chambers, with Senate Democrats holding at least 54 seats after long-shot pickups in South Carolina, Texas and Kansas, and they plan a 100-day agenda on gas, grocery and health care costs alongside broad oversight of the Trump administration, with impeachment an option. Trump signaled he could work with Democrats while threatening vetoes and acknowledged the Iran war affected the vote, and Vice President JD Vance pointedly wrote that "The reason we lost is the war". House Speaker Mike Johnson will not seek reelection as GOP leader, according to two people familiar with his decision, setting up a potentially brutal leadership fight as some races remain too early to call.

item.title: Blake Moore will run again in leadership despite GOP midterm losses
item.description:
Utah Rep. Blake Moore plans to seek reelection as House Republican conference vice chairman in next week's leadership elections, though he is also vying to be the top Republican on the House Budget Committee and said "I would not serve as both". item.title: Mayor Karen Bass and democratic socialist Nithya Raman in tight race to lead Los Angeles
item.description:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass and council member Nithya Raman, a challenger backed by the Democratic Socialists of America, were in a tight race in early returns Wednesday, with Raman holding a slim advantage and an estimated one-third of ballots still uncounted. Bass, backed by Gavin Newsom, Kamala Harris and Nancy Pelosi, has called Raman "not ready for primetime" and her views on policing and homelessness extreme, while Raman has pledged to cut the number of people sleeping in tents and encampments by at least 50% by 2028. The incumbent still faces fallout from the 2025 Palisades Fire, and a Raman win would place her alongside New York's Zohran Mamdani among democratic socialists leading city governments.

item.title: County commissions in Weber, Davis counties will each get 2 new members
item.description:
The Davis and Weber county commissions will each gain two new members after Tuesday's election, with former Bountiful Mayor Kendalyn Harris and former Plain City Mayor Jon Beesley having run unopposed for open seats. The other two races were still being counted: in Davis County, unaffiliated former commissioner Bret Millburn narrowly led Republican Susan Lee 50.7% to 49.3%, though Millburn noted as many as 30,000 ballots remain uncounted, and in Weber County, Republican Duane Kearsley led Democrat Alvin Thurgood 49.2% to 45.2%. Harris, who will take the seat Bob Stevenson left to run for the Utah House, said the first priority is to "get our fiscal house in order".

item.title: CVS to split into two companies, in major breakup of its $117B healthcare empire
item.description:
CVS Health will separate into two companies in a tax-free transaction expected to close in early 2028, reversing a strategy that began with its 2007 Caremark merger and continued with its $69 billion purchase of Aetna in 2018. CEO David Joyner described the move as "taking what I believe is one great company and making it two," and the split isn't expected to change how people shop at CVS or what patients pay for prescriptions. It cuts against an industry trend toward integrated conglomerates that consumer advocates and lawmakers blame for higher costs, and CVS shares fell 10% in early trading even as the company reported stronger third-quarter results and raised its guidance.

item.title: First lady Abby Cox wrote a children's book
item.description:
Utah first lady Abby Cox read her new children's book, Jennie Makes Room, to students in the Governor's Mansion ballroom, telling the story of philanthropist Jennie Judge Kearns, whose giving helped fund an orphanage that became Kearns-Saint Ann Catholic School, helped finance the Cathedral of the Madeleine and supplied the mansion now used as the governor's residence. Cox said she "realized how much my work intersected with the things that she was passionate about", and said proceeds will go to the Mansion Foundation to preserve the home, whose details are hidden throughout Matt Loveridge's illustrations. The school's principal, a great-great-granddaughter of Kearns, noted that the students were walking through the home of the family whose generosity helped make their school possible.

item.title: Progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Senate race, will be first Muslim senator
item.description:
Progressive Abdul El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers for Michigan's open Senate seat and will become the nation's first Muslim senator, after a grassroots campaign built on Medicare for All and sharp criticism of Israel that survived nearly $30 million in AIPAC spending against him in the primary. Rogers struggled to stay aligned with Trump amid high fuel prices and an unpopular war with Iran, while Republicans sought to link El-Sayed to terrorist organizations without evidence. "They might have been pointing to my name and my faith, but we all know my name and my faith are not why you can't afford your gas," El-Sayed said in his victory speech, a result that gives progressives an argument heading into 2028 that their agenda can win in battleground states.
